title: Senate panel wants Bato to explain prolonged absence
summary: The Senate ethics committee is set to call a hearing on the complaint filed against Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa over his prolonged absence from official duties in the chamber, committee…

blocks.text: Sen. Ronald Dela Rosa talks to media at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay, Metro Manila on May 13, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate ethics committee is set to call a hearing on the complaint filed against Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa over his prolonged absence from official duties in the chamber, committee chairman Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III confirmed yesterday.
In an official committee document uploaded by group Wag Kang KuCorrupt, Sotto informed Dela Rosa that the complaint against him was “compliant in form and substance.”
Sotto confirmed that he sent a formal letter to Dela Rosa last Oct. 22, giving him 15 days to respond to the complaint filed by the group represented by Barry Gutierrez, Cielo Magno and others.
“Yes, that’s a letter I sent Sen. Dela Rosa,” Sotto told reporters via text message when asked to verify the document.
With the 15-day period having lapsed, Sotto noted that the committee’s schedule has been delayed by other major proceedings in the chamber.
“I will call a hearing soon. Budget and impeachment just getting in the way,” he said.
Asked whether Dela Rosa or his lawyer had submitted a reply to the notice, Sotto said he would verify the status of the submission.

According to the Oct. 22 letter signed by Sotto, the ethics panel met in an executive session on the same day and found the complaint, as supplemented, “in substantial compliance, both in form and in substance, with Section 17” of the committee rules.

Pursuant to Section 18(C) of the rules, the committee formally transmitted the complaint to Dela Rosa and invited him to provide “any information relevant to the complaint, including a written response, within fifteen (15) days from receipt of this notice.”
The complaint was originally filed on Feb. 25, 2026 and the committee informed Dela Rosa of the filing on April 28.
On May 4, the panel returned the complaint to the complainants for failure to substantially comply with Section 17 of the rules, prompting the group to file supplemental affidavits on Sept. 14.
